title: McGuinness Boulevard: official 2026 evaluation and identification audit
status: Observed before/after descriptive evidence; causal effect on all-mode person flow and complete journey time remains unidentified

treatment_definition.geography: Calyer St to Pulaski Bridge; April 2026 map labels Freeman–Calyer late 2023
treatment_definition.capacity: One permanent moving lane and a second daytime moving lane per direction; second lane becomes parking overnight
treatment_definition.weekday_weekend_detail: 2023 cabinet minutes confirm clock hours but not weekday/weekend/holiday exceptions. September 2024 proposed-design slide3 mentions most overnight and weekend parking; obtain as-built signs before encoding day-of-week exposure.
treatment_definition.hours_source: DOT liaison report to September 21, 2023 District Service Cabinet, included in October 11 CB1 minutes PDF p140: northern construction starting; 07:00–19:00 two moving lanes each direction; 19:00–07:00 one lane

treatment_definition.construction_start_interval: Preparation in week preceding 2024-11-02 announcement; major roadway reconfiguration scheduled 2024-11-04; several weeks, weather permitting
treatment_definition.capacity: One moving lane per direction throughout the day
cointerventions: Later punch-list work and connecting conventional bike lanes
treatment_definition.note: September 2024 slide 3 showed the earlier proposed daytime two-lane design. Do not use that proposal as the implemented southern design; November construction notice supersedes it.

treatment_definition.design: One moving lane all day in each direction; existing left-turn bays maintained; parking-protected bike lanes, seven shorter crossings, turning treatments and loading/parking changes
treatment_definition.capacity_change: Removal of existing daytime-only second moving lane; no corresponding overnight reduction in nominal moving-lane count
treatment_definition.bicycle_baseline: Bike lanes already existed from 2023; wider/parking-protected configuration replaces earlier barrier/rush-hour-lane arrangement
treatment_definition.estimand: Incremental daytime capacity/curb/protection package; not first introduction of bike access
treatment_definition.note: An announced or expected construction completion is not an observed treatment activation date. Obtain segment-level sign/marking completion logs.

evidence.window: Two weeks of midweek ATR data in Fall; exact dates and AM/PM peak durations unstated
evidence.author_report: Southern vehicle volumes down 100–400 during peak times; northern volumes increased; Manhattan unchanged; Leonard/Humboldt increased but within street capacity
evidence.what_it_measures: Vehicles at separate cross-sections, not people or complete trips
evidence.reason: Northern and southern locations are serial sections of the same corridor; summing can double-count vehicles, and no aligned parallel-street counts or boundary accounting is supplied

evidence.geography: McGuinness between Green and Freeman, both directions
evidence.window: Two-week average ATRs counted in October/November
evidence.extraction: Illustrative descriptive digitization, not raw observations: 93 vector bars per direction per year; tick labels suggest 15-minute time grid from 00:00 to 23:00; digitized values rounded to nearest 10
evidence.raw_window_semantics: Unknown whether hourly rolling windows, annualized 15-minute counts, or another smoothing/aggregation; do not sum bars as independent counts
author_reports: Southbound AM volumes lower in 2025 than 2021
Southbound and PM peak volumes lower in 2023 than 2021
Southbound PM volumes higher in 2025 than 2023
evidence.causal_use: Time-of-day description and potential exposure checks, not sufficient independent pretrends or a causal daytime-versus-night effect

evidence.window: One hour; date and clock hour not stated
limitations: All-bicycle count, not Citi Bike share
Cannot identify newly induced cycling versus rerouting
No defensible all-mode sum with the motor charts

evidence.status: Period ambiguous in an April 2026 presentation; do not treat as full calendar-year comparison or silently change years
evidence.next_step: Recalculate equal-period counts from raw continuous-counter data and obtain DOT clarification

evidence.geography: Whole McGuinness segment Meeker Ave to Pulaski Bridge
evidence.comparison_label: Longer than previous years after southern installation; not a supplied formal estimate with specified reference year and uncertainty
limitations: Whole-corridor segment time, not southern-only time
INRIX sample size/composition and weighting unknown
No access, parking, waiting, transfers or complete journey times

evidence.window: October/November; 2019 missing on some smaller streets, including Humboldt
printed_graphs: Manhattan Ave NB Meeker to Freeman
Greenpoint Ave WB Kingsland to West St
evidence.qualification: Appendix acknowledges some BQE southbound midday travel-time increase, not similarly observed in January/February 2025
evidence.control_role: Potential diversion outcomes; exclude from an untreated control pool unless spillover exposure can be ruled out

evidence.condition: 30–40% AM/PM peak vehicle-volume reduction would be required to preserve existing level of service after northern lane removal
evidence.other_report: More than 30% of McGuinness vehicles have neither origin nor destination in Greenpoint; method not supplied
evidence.adaptation: DOT anticipates initial delay and diversion, with ongoing signal, loading/curb and marking changes

source_inconsistency.summary_claim: Traffic has not shifted to adjacent neighborhood streets
source_inconsistency.qualifying_detail: Leonard St and Humboldt St vehicle volumes increased
source_inconsistency.interpretation: Do not repeat the blanket summary as evidence of no diversion; raw counts and a formal comparison are needed to determine magnitude and cause

transit_coverage.B62: No passenger counts, load profiles, speed or journey-time series in evaluation
transit_coverage.B48: No passenger counts, load profiles, speed or journey-time series in evaluation
transit_coverage.G_subway: No ridership or journey-time series in evaluation
transit_coverage.7_subway: No ridership or journey-time series in evaluation
transit_coverage.bus_facility: CB1 PDF p65 / slide30 depicts southbound bus boarding island near Freeman/Pulaski; this is a design element, not a measured bus benefit

proposed_causal_design.primary_target: Network/OD-area effect of the implemented redesign package on person throughput and passenger-weighted complete journey time
proposed_causal_design.2024_design: Controlled event-study or synthetic comparison using unaffected matched corridors, pretrends and donor exclusion for spillovers; distinguish phases and exclude construction windows
proposed_causal_design.2026_time_of_day_contrast: Northern before/after change during former second-lane hours minus overnight change, then subtract the same day/night contrast on external comparison corridors
why_not_yet_identified: Exact treatment completion and sign-hours unknown
Off-hours receive protection/parking/pedestrian changes even if moving-lane count is stable
Daytime/nighttime demand and mode shares may have different trends
Continuous before/after raw counts are missing
Concurrent network, transit and policy changes need adjustment
proposed_causal_design.appropriate_claim_if_successful: Daytime treatment effect MINUS nighttime treatment effect of the northern redesign package, under parallel changes in the day–night outcome gap relative to comparison corridors. This identifies the daytime effect alone only if the nighttime effect is zero or independently identified.
proposed_causal_design.inappropriate_claim: A pure isolated effect of adding a bike lane, or an instrumental-variable estimate using daytime availability as an exclusion-valid instrument
proposed_causal_design.capacity_vs_realized_flow: Observed count reductions can reflect rerouting, mode substitution, suppressed trips or timing changes; demonstrate saturated-flow conditions before interpreting counts as road capacity

network_aggregation.reason: No aligned common-boundary all-mode counts, occupancies or complete-journey time samples. Counting the same traveler at northern/southern sections or a bike-to-subway transfer twice would inflate totals.
network_aggregation.required_design: Predefine a common screenline/catchment and count each crossing once, or use person-linked OD journeys. Report local cross-section flow separately from network completed-trip throughput.

priority_data_requests: DOT raw ATR interval files underlying April2026 slide11 and appendix34–36: dates/times, location IDs, directions, interval semantics, vehicle classification, quality/missingness flags, aggregation code; include Leonard, Humboldt, Manhattan and all parallel crossings
DOT raw bicycle observation sheets underlying slide12: exact day/hour, direction, sidewalk/street, count protocol and weather; obtain aligned motor/bus/walking observations
DOT/INRIX raw segment travel-time samples and aggregation definitions for main and diversion corridors in 2019 and 2021–2026, exact geometries, sample sizes, vehicle classes and quality fields
DOT segment-level actual 2023/2024/2026 markings/sign activation dates, as-built weekday/weekend/holiday regulations and signal/curb modification dates
MTA B62/B48 stop-to-stop APC passenger loads and AVL travel/wait times across the same boundary/time windows; route/service-change histories
MTA G/7 station-hour entries plus route OD allocation, loads and wait/runtime/transfer distributions; distinguish station entries from screenline passenger flow
Person-level travel diary or privacy-preserving consenting OD panel linking complete trips and modes, so car-to-subway substitution and door-to-door time are measurable
Vehicle occupancy samples by class/direction/time and matched traffic saturation/queue indicators; do not assume each vehicle equals one person
Clarification of the Pulaski 11%/123000 reporting dates and the no-neighborhood-shift summary versus Leonard/Humboldt increases
